papers.title: Interpretable Machine Learning-Assisted design of refractory High-Entropy alloys with balanced strength and plasticity
papers.abstract: The vast compositional space of refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) makes it challenging to identify compositions with balanced room temperature strength and plasticity. Here, an interpretable machine-learning-assisted strategy is developed to predict yield strength and fracture strain using separate regression models. The optimized LightGBM and random forest models achieve test-set R 2 values of 0.80 and 0.84 for yield strength and fracture strain, respectively. Descriptor-based SHAP analysis identifies property-dependent predictive associations, while an auxiliary composition-based model provides elemental SHAP information to inform the composition search bounds. Three designed alloys exhibit room temperature yield strengths of 1310–1430 MPa and fracture strains of 15.8–21.7%. Among them, Nb 30 Mo 17 Ta 24 Hf 15 Zr 14 (A2) achieves a yield strength of 1370 MPa and a fracture strain of 18.0%. Additional compression tests at 1000 °C show that this alloy exhibits a yield strength of approximately 940 MPa and reaches a true compressive strain of at least 35% without fracture. TEM and EDS observations reveal Zr-Hf-rich particles near locally curved dislocations, suggesting a possible contribution of particle-dislocation interactions to deformation resistance. These findings support interpretable machine learning as a tool for identifying RHEAs with balanced room temperature strength and plasticity and highlight the promising compressive performance of the A2 alloy at 1000 °C.

papers.title: Predicting grain growth evolution under complex thermal profiles with deep learning through thermal descriptor modulation
papers.abstract: Predicting microstructure evolution during thermomechanical treatment is essential for determining the final mechanical properties of a material, yet conventional simulations based on Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) remain computationally expensive. Our prior Deep Learning (DL) framework using Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (ConvLSTM) has proven effective in accelerating grain growth prediction, though its applicability was limited to constant-temperature or single-rate thermal profiles. As the model was trained exclusively under constant thermal conditions, it cannot account for the thermal history dependence of grain boundary kinetics, fundamentally limiting its applicability to the time-varying thermal profiles characteristic of industrial heat treatment processes. This study extends the previous framework by incorporating Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) for thermal conditioning to predict grain growth under complex, time-varying thermal profiles. The model was trained on a large dataset of grain growth evolution under thermal profiles with heating and cooling rates ranging from 0.01 kelvin per second to 10 kelvin per second. The results demonstrate that the proposed thermal conditioning mechanism enables the model to capture the influence of variable thermal profiles on grain boundary migration kinetics. Across the three test scenarios of increasing complexity, the model achieved a Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of up to 0.93 and mean grain size error below 3.2%. Despite the architectural extensions, inference time remains on the order of seconds per prediction sequence, preserving the computational advantage over PDE-based simulations.
